spec.name: News tone v5
spec.notes: Long names with improving news sentiment.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.9, annual return 6%, maximum drawdown 5%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.92 to -0.02 (change -1.94).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.92 to 1.92. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.51 (as submitted, 5 bps: 1.92); it breaks even at 28.5 bps with daily turnover 0.10.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.92 against 1.92 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -0.82 against 1.92 in research, a gap of +2.74.
The best year gives 22% of total P&L (year 1) and calm regimes give 78%; Sharpe is 2.44 in calm and 1.23 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.04, so the claimed 1.90 becomes 1.86 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.33 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.00, 95th percentile 0.58).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.92 to as low as 0.57 (as low as 1.12 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 39% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 23% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (lag_test EX-1, holdout_test EX-5).
